The subject names its justification exactly: 'Live G02 occupancy. artifactPathWhenAuthored.' Assuming the highest version number is live would have flagged a correct citation as wrong. Second, the forbidden constant. 83886080 appears eight times, which a sweep would flag — but the constant originates in the live text, where exactByteIntent itself ends 'It does not pin 83886080 as an authorized threshold', and all eight subject occurrences are refusals of the same kind. The sharper form of that attack is the MB form: live threshold.bound reads 'immutable installed tree ≤ 80 MB' and live passProperty reads 'Size comparison to 80 MB is scored only after a D-006 unit-and-accounting successor'. MB is how the live text expresses the bound at all, so carrying it forward would sit closer to authorizing than repeating the refused byte value. All thirteen states are exact substrings: twelve of exactByteIntent and the thirteenth of passProperty, and the subject's source field for that one correctly reads 'G02 v1 passProperty' rather than exactByteIntent — it distinguishes the two live fields rather than attributing everything to one. The 4x3+1 shape follows the live text, which is explicitly 'Per platform:' with three items, while the shared-executable condition is stated once in passProperty. One coherence result worth naming: OBL-2 is open for exactly the reason the unit prohibition exists — the live core-gate chain records 'OBL-2 is not closed while D-006 MB unit and G02 tree accounting remain UNDECIDED' — so the two prohibitions are the same leftover from two sides, and the refusal to invent a unit is what makes 'Does not close OBL-2' substantive.
